title: Long-lived client secret in CI
summary: A pipeline authenticates with a service principal secret stored as a repository secret. The secret works from anywhere until it expires, often years later, and any leak gives an attacker the same access.
notes: Secrets leak through logs, forks, compromised actions, and copies on developers' machines. Nothing ties a client secret to the pipeline that is supposed to use it.
Fix: workload identity federation. GitHub's short-lived OIDC token replaces the secret, and the federated credential pins which repo and environment may use the identity.
Until you can migrate: short expiry, one secret per pipeline, and alerts on service principal sign-ins from unexpected locations.

nodes.label: AZURE_CREDENTIALS (repo secret)
nodes.warning: Long-lived, replayable bearer secret: whoever holds it is the service principal.
